name: Silicon Effects on Root Exudates and Rhizosphere Enzyme Activity in Grain Crops
description: Meta-analysis of how silicon (Si) supplementation affects root exudate composition (organic acids, sugars, amino acids) and rhizosphere enzyme activity (acid phosphatase, phytase, urease) in grain crops. Mechanistic companion to the root architecture meta-analysis. Core question: does Si drive chemical mobilization of sparingly soluble phosphorus through increased organic acid exudation and phosphatase activity?
intervention: Silicon supplementation (any form: sodium silicate, potassium silicate, calcium silicate, amorphous silica, diatomaceous earth, slag, rice husk ash, silicic acid)
control: No silicon application (0 Si, -Si, control, untreated)
primary_outcomes: Citric acid / citrate exudation rate (µmol g-1 root h-1 or µmol plant-1 d-1)
Acid phosphatase activity in rhizosphere soil or root (µmol p-nitrophenol g-1 h-1 or nmol g-1 min-1)
Phytase activity in rhizosphere soil or root
secondary_outcomes: Rhizosphere pH (acidification relative to bulk soil)
Soil available P in rhizosphere (mg/kg, Olsen/Bray — as proxy for exudate-driven P release)
typical_effect_size: +20% to +100% increase in organic acid exudation and phosphatase activity based on preliminary literature (Zhang et al. 2025, Neu et al. 2017)
important_moderators: Phosphorus source type (CRITICAL: soluble P / KH2PO4 vs iron phosphate / FePO4 vs hydroxyapatite / Ca-P vs rock phosphate vs P-deficient — does Si boost exudates MORE under insoluble P?)
P availability level (adequate vs deficient vs severely deficient)
Soil pH (pH<6 = Fe-Al-P dominant, pH>7 = Ca-P/hydroxyapatite dominant, pH 6-7 = mixed)
Soil calcareous status (calcareous yes/no, CaCO3 % — calcareous = hydroxyapatite context)
Specific exudate measured (citrate vs malate vs oxalate vs total OA vs phosphatase vs phytase)
Grain species (wheat/Triticum, rice/Oryza, barley/Hordeum, maize/Zea mays, sorghum, millet, oat, rye)
Measurement location (root surface exudate collection vs bulk rhizosphere soil vs root-free soil)
Growth stage at measurement (seedling, vegetative, reproductive)
Duration of Si treatment before measurement (days)
extraction_priorities: 1. CRITICAL: Extract EACH exudate/enzyme variable separately — citrate, malate, oxalate, acid phosphatase, alkaline phosphatase, phytase are all separate observations
2. CRITICAL: Record P source and soil pH — the key question is whether Si boosts exudates MORE under insoluble P (hydroxyapatite, FePO4) than soluble P
3. Control = zero Si or no-Si under the SAME P conditions
4. In factorial designs (Si x P source x CO2), extract EACH combination separately
5. Get variance (SD/SE/LSD/SEM) and sample size (n) for every observation
6. Note measurement method: root washing/collection, root exudate trap, rhizosphere soil extraction, enzymatic assay
7. Note units carefully — exudate rates vary widely (per g root FW, per g root DW, per plant, per pot)
8. Rhizosphere pH: extract as absolute pH value AND as delta vs bulk soil if reported
9. SOIL DATA: Extract pH, CaCO3 (%), OM (%), available P (mg/kg), Fe/Al oxides if reported

10. INFERRED P FORM: Same decision tree as root architecture meta-analysis — (a) explicit label first; (b) calcareous/pH>7 = Ca-P_hydroxyapatite; (c) pH<6 = Fe-Al-P; (d) pH 6-7 = mixed; (e) hydroponic full nutrient = soluble_P; (f) P-deficient = P_deficient; (g) else unknown

inferred_dominant_P_form.description: Dominant P mineral form inferred from explicit label or soil chemistry — same classification as root architecture meta-analysis for cross-meta-analysis comparability

categories.Ca-P_hydroxyapatite: Calcareous soil (CaCO3>1%), alkaline (pH>7), or explicit hydroxyapatite/Ca-P source
categories.Fe-Al-P: Acid soil (pH<6), or explicit FePO4/Al-phosphate source
categories.mixed_pH_neutral: Neutral soil pH 6-7, no calcareous description, no explicit P source
categories.soluble_P: Hydroponic or pot with soluble P fertilizer (KH2PO4, NaH2PO4) at adequate supply

inferred_dominant_P_form.inference_priority: Explicit P label > calcareous description > CaCO3% > soil pH > soil type > unknown

exudate_class.description: Classification of the measured compound into functional group

categories.organic_acid_carboxylate: Citrate, malate, oxalate, succinate, fumarate, tartrate — direct P solubilizers via ligand exchange and acidification
categories.phosphatase_enzyme: Acid phosphatase, alkaline phosphatase, phytase — mineralize organic P
categories.rhizosphere_pH: Bulk or rhizosphere soil pH measurement
categories.available_P_proxy: Olsen-P, Bray-P, or CaCl2-extractable P in rhizosphere soil — indirect measure of exudate-driven P release
categories.other_exudate: Sugars, amino acids, phenolics, other measured exudates

tc_confusion_warnings: Control is ZERO-SI under same P conditions — not a different P source
Rhizosphere soil assays and root surface assays are different measurement locations — record which one
Phosphatase units vary widely: p-nitrophenol µmol/g/h, nmol/g/min, µg/g/h — extract exact units
Some papers report exudates per gram root DW, others per gram FW, others per plant — record units precisely
Citric acid and citrate are the same compound — record as citrate
Total OA is not the sum of individual acids in all papers — if total is given, record separately from individual acids
Some papers measure rhizosphere soil enzyme activity, others measure root-bound phosphatase — note the distinction
Hydroponic root exudate collection (root wash method) gives very different absolute values than soil studies — study_type is critical

population.description: Grain crops (cereals and grasses grown for grain)

primary.description: Root exudate composition and rhizosphere enzyme activity

benchmark.notes: No published meta-analysis on Si x root exudates in grain crops — novel synthesis

inclusion_criteria: Grain crop species (wheat, rice, barley, maize, sorghum, millet, oat, rye)
At least one quantitative exudate or enzyme measurement (organic acid rate, phosphatase activity, rhizosphere pH)
Quantitative data with mean and variance OR extractable from figure
exclusion_criteria: Exudate data only qualitative (presence/absence, gene expression only)
No variance data and not extractable from figure

subgroup_analyses.primary: P source type (soluble vs FePO4 vs hydroxyapatite vs rock phosphate vs P-deficient) — does Si boost exudates MORE under insoluble P?
secondary: Exudate class (organic acid vs phosphatase vs rhizosphere pH)
Specific compound (citrate vs malate vs oxalate vs acid phosphatase vs phytase)
Study type (hydroponic vs pot vs field)
subgroup_analyses.cross_meta_analysis_note: Use same inferred_dominant_P_form classification as root architecture meta-analysis to enable direct comparison of Si effects on physical (root architecture) vs chemical (exudates/enzymes) P-mobilization mechanisms across P source types
